column1: # THE FLAW WAS THE FILTER. "Dispatches offsets 48, 52 and 56" counts the ARMS OF
# A JUMP TABLE as separate call sites. A switch over virtual slots looks exactly
# like a caller of several of them, and two of the four candidates were nothing
# but that.
# FILTER 3 -- the setters' SIGNATURE, which should have been first: a dispatch at
# 48, 52 or 56 with BOTH f1 and f2 set in the surrounding instructions. Thirteen
# sites in eight functions, and none of them is a switch arm, because a jump
# table does not set up arguments per arm.
# function
# 0x82290E20 is the strongest candidate on shape alone -- four sites across two
# different setters, one caller -- and NONE of the eight has been read. The
# invented link in demo_flight_input.h stays invented until one of them is.
# CYCLE 1400: the first of the eight, read.
# 0x82290E20 IS A GENUINE CALLER. Its five dispatch sites have the setters'
# signature exactly:
#     lwz  r10,0(r29)        the object's vtable
#     fmr  f1,f31            the INCREMENT
#     mr   r3,r29            this
#     lfs  f2,2092(r11)      the TARGET
#     lwz  r11,48(r10)       slot 12   (or 56, slot 14)
#     mtctr / bctrl
#     clrlwi r11,r3,24       the return code, tested
# which CONFIRMS CYCLE 1393 FROM THE CALLER'S SIDE. That cycle derived f1 =
# increment and f2 = target by reading the setters; this reads a caller that
# shares no code with them and agrees. Third mapping in this campaign met from
# both ends, after float_slot_for_bit (1353) and the accumulator crossing (1393).
# BUT IT IS NOT THE INPUT PATH. Every one of its five sites passes
#     f2 = 0.0        (0x8200082C, the image's zero, via f30)
# so this function only ever commands LEVEL. It is a recovery or auto-level
# behaviour, not stick steering, and on a changed return it increments a counter
# at [r30+744]. Its constants fit that reading: pi/3 (0x82069C28, and it IS
# float32(pi/3), not a decimal literal -- checked, unlike the four traps this
# subsystem has produced), 0.95, 0.5 and 500.0 are thresholds.
# Its only caller is 0x822931B0, unread.
# SEVEN OF THE EIGHT REMAIN. The demo's invented link is unchanged.
# CYCLE 1401: the remaining seven, separated by what f2 carries.
# One line per candidate was the promised discriminator, and it splits them:

# 0x82366AA0 IS REFUTED BY ARGUMENT COUNT, and that is a discriminator worth
# keeping. It reads a state at [+28], advances 9 -> 10, then dispatches offset
# 52 with
# -- FOUR arguments. The command setters take exactly (this, f1, f2); cycle
# 1393's differential compared r3, the accumulator, the target field and the flag
# byte across thirty cases and no fourth argument appears anywhere in their 45
# instructions. So this dispatches a different class's slot 52, and its +36 and
# +44 are that class's fields rather than the flight model's accumulators, which
# happen to sit at the same displacements.
# The fifth displacement collision this thread has caught, and the first caught
# by an ARGUMENT COUNT rather than by a class filter.
# STILL NOT FOUND: whatever turns a stick into a command. Four candidates remain
# unread (0x822911E8, 0x821405F8, 0x822389D8, and 0x82290500's non-zero site).
# CYCLE 1402: the class map, run BEFORE reading.

# whose_vtable.py first, the listing second. Cycle 1383 was caught not checking

column1: # So the two candidates the class map CAN name are both refuted, and the six it
# cannot are direct-call functions in 0x8229xxxx and 0x8223xxxx. Three of those
# six are the auto-level subsystem (cycles 1400, 1401).
# UNREAD: 0x822911E8 (538 insns, four callers, f2 from a field and a computed
# value) and 0x822389D8 (589 insns, mixed). Those two are the search.
# CYCLE 1403: the search from the other end, and why it stops.
# 0x822911E8 dispatches slot 14 with
# -- f1 = 1.0, f2 = a field of an object reached through [r30+672]. Data-driven,
# and its constants are +-pi/6 and +-pi/12 (30 and 15 degrees) with 0.97, 0.9,
# 400.0, 150.0 and 7200.0. Commanded attitude angles from a table: an AI or
# navigation repertoire is at least as good a reading as a stick, and NOTHING
# here distinguishes them.
# SO THE SEARCH WAS RUN FROM THE INPUT SIDE INSTEAD. The contracted input record
# array is 0x826EDB98, materialised at nine sites in nine functions:
# Forward from all nine, following direct calls, four hops, 128 functions
# explored: NO PATH to any of the eleven candidates.
# AND THAT NEGATIVE IS WEAK, for a reason this file must state rather than let a
# reader over-read. Cycle 1218 measured that `bl` plus non-local `b` reaches
# 2,144 of 8,135 functions -- ABOUT A QUARTER of this program. The thirteenth
# shape. Everything else is reached through vtables, and the input path's own
# consumer 0x82211C10 is called through one.
# So the search is blocked from BOTH ends by the same property: the setters are
# dispatched virtually at slot numbers 78-151 unrelated functions share, and the
# input side reaches its consumers virtually too. Neither end offers a handle
# that a call-graph walk can follow.
# THE DECISION. The search stops here. The demo's link stays invented and its
# header says so. What would resume it, in order of cost:
#   1. read 0x822389D8, the last unread candidate;
#   2. micro-execute 0x822911E8 on a synthetic object and see whether [r30+672]
#      can be made to point at anything input-shaped -- a capsule answers "what
#      does this read" where a call graph cannot;
#   3. accept that the player's commands may not pass through these setters at
#      all, and look instead for a SECOND writer of [+36]/[+40]/[+44] outside the
#      class family, which cycle 1393's search deliberately excluded.
# (3) is the one this file would bet on, and it is the one nobody has run.
